content: 1. Ferric Maltol: To avoid significant effects on the safety or efficacy of ferric maltol, administer it separately from other drugs. The duration of separation depends on the absorption characteristics of the concomitant medication, such as time to peak concentration and whether it is an immediate or extended-release product. 2. Belladonna Alkaloids and Fesoterodine: Both decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Phenobarbital reduces fesoterodine levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Fexinidazole and Phenobarbital: Fexinidazole increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Conversely, phenobarbital reduces fexinidazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. Fexinidazole metabolites (M1 and M2) are associated with QT prolongation risks. 4. Phenobarbital and Fexofenadine: Phenobarbital decreases fexofenadine levels by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 5. Phenobarbital and Finasteride: Phenobarbital reduces finasteride levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 6. Phenobarbital and Finerenone: Phenobarbital decreases finerenone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the potential for serious interactions. 7. Belladonna Alkaloids and Flavoxate: Both decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Phenobarbital and Flibanserin: Phenobarbital reduces flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease flibanserin systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Phenobarbital and Fluconazole: Phenobarbital decreases fluconazole levels by reducing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 10. Phenobarbital and Fludrocortisone: Phenobarbital reduces fludrocortisone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Belladonna Alkaloids and Fluphenazine: Belladonna alkaloids reduce fluphenazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Fluphenazine increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids via pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Phenobarbital and Flurazepam: Both increase sedation. Phenobarbital also reduces flurazepam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. 13. Phenobarbital and Flurbiprofen: Phenobarbital reduces flurbiprofen levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 14. Phenobarbital and Fluticasone: Phenobarbital reduces fluticasone levels (both inhaled and furoate forms) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Phenobarbital and Fluvastatin: Phenobarbital reduces fluvastatin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 16. Folic Acid and Phenobarbital: Folic acid reduces phenobarbital levels by increasing its metabolism, while phenobarbital reduces folic acid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 17. Phenobarbital and Fondaparinux: Phenobarbital reduces fondaparinux effects by increasing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. 18. Phenobarbital and Formoterol: Phenobarbital increases sedation, while formoterol decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 19. Phenobarbital and Fosamprenavir: Phenobarbital reduces fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Phenobarbital and Fosphenytoin: Phenobarbital reduces fosphenytoin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 21. Phenobarbital and Fostamatinib: Phenobarbital reduces fostamatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. 22. Phenobarbital and Fostemsavir: Phenobarbital reduces fostemsavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance. 23. Phenobarbital and Frovatriptan: Phenobarbital reduces frovatriptan levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 24. Phenobarbital and Fruquintinib: Phenobarbital reduces fruquintinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. 25. Phenobarbital and Furosemide: Phenobarbital reduces furosemide levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 26. Belladonna Alkaloids and Galantamine: Galantamine increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 27. Phenobarbital and Ganaxolone: Phenobarbital reduces ganaxolone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose but do not exceed the maximum daily dose for weight. 28. Phenobarbital and Gefitinib: Phenobarbital reduces gefitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase gefitinib to 500 mg daily if coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer, and resume the standard dose 7 days after discontinuing the inducer. 29. Phenobarbital and Gentamicin: Phenobarbital reduces gentamicin levels by enhancing P-glycoprotein efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Phenobarbital and Gilteritinib: Phenobarbital reduces gilteritinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. 31. Phenobarbital and Glasdegib: Phenobarbital reduces glasdegib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 32. Phenobarbital and Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Phenobarbital reduces glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Phenobarbital and Glyburide: Phenobarbital reduces glyburide levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Belladonna Alkaloids and Glycopyrrolate: Both decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Phenobarbital and Gotu Kola: Gotu kola enhances phenobarbital effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Phenobarbital and Green Tea: Phenobarbital reduces green tea levels by increasing its metabolism. Green tea products may contain caffeine, and barbiturates can increase caffeine metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 37. Phenobarbital and Griseofulvin: Phenobarbital reduces griseofulvin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 38. Phenobarbital and Guanfacine: Phenobarbital reduces guanfacine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. For ADHD patients, consider doubling the guanfacine dose if coadministered with a CYP3A4 inducer. 39. Phenobarbital and Guselkumab: Guselkumab may alter CYP450 enzyme formation due to increased cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. Monitor closely for therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing guselkumab in patients receiving CYP450 substrates. 40. Belladonna Alkaloids and Haloperidol: Haloperidol increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergism. Both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids reduce haloperidol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Phenobarbital and Hawthorn: Hawthorn enhances phenobarbital effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Phenobarbital and Hemin: Phenobarbital reduces hemin effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may decrease hemin efficacy. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Belladonna Alkaloids and Henbane: Both decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Phenobarbital and Heparin: Phenobarbital reduces heparin effects by increasing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. 45. Belladonna Alkaloids and Homatropine: Both decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Phenobarbital and Hops: Hops enhance phenobarbital effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Belladonna Alkaloids and Huperzine A: Huperzine A increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 48. Phenobarbital and Hydrocodone: Phenobarbital reduces hydrocodone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. 49. Phenobarbital and Hydrocortisone: Phenobarbital reduces hydrocortisone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Phenobarbital and Hydromorphone: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Phenobarbital and Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Phenobarbital reduces hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Phenobarbital and Hydroxyzine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Belladonna Alkaloids and Hyoscyamine: Both decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Phenobarbital and Ibrutinib: Phenobarbital reduces ibrutinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. 55. Phenobarbital and Ibuprofen: Phenobarbital reduces ibuprofen levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor.
